correctness.rationale: For one reused observation rather than independent fresh iteration noise, the geometric sum gives c_i(K)=sigma^2/lambda_i (1-(1-omega lambda_i)^K)^2. For lambda_i>lambda_j the derivative of log(c_i/c_j)/2 is alpha/(exp(alpha t)-1)-beta/(exp(beta t)-1)<0 for alpha>beta>0; the u=0 endpoint follows by a limit. At t=1 the ratio is lambda_i/lambda_j>1; at infinity its reciprocal is below 1. The filter F_K(z)=(1-(1-z)^K)^2/z for 0<z<=1 has a unique maximum, since its derivative changes sign once when sum_{h=0}^{K-1}(1-z)^(-h)=2K (K>=2), with K=1 monotone. Therefore its sampled spectral variances are unimodal; top-r indices admit a consecutive block. Strict crossing excludes moving a smaller index into a later optimum while a larger index departs. A two-level spectrum proves late retained-trace ratio mu/L. Independent exact rational 4-mode windows were {1,2}, {2,3}, {3,4} at K=1,10,100, and 5,200 bounded numerical rank-window checks across 100 new random spectra passed. Finite checks do not prove the continuous all-spectrum statements.
